svg.title: Wi-Fi on the communicator, mockups
svg.text: Wi-Fi · communicator
T-LoRa Pager, 480×222, drawn at 2×. Turn moves, press selects, Backspace goes back.
Joining a network

Device › Wi-Fi turns the station on and off and joins networks on the device itself, keyboard and all. Saved networks join by themselves, as on a phone. A phone can do the same over ULCP and is never needed.
1 · Device, Wi-Fi focused
Wi-Fi sits after Bluetooth, on boards with a station. Its value is the network it is on, and nothing otherwise.
2 · Off
Only the switch. Off powers the station down and forgets nothing. Turned on, it joins a saved network in range by itself.
3 · On, nothing saved
Opening the screen while on scans once. Networks appear as they are heard, one row per name, strongest first; the dots beside
Nearby spin until the scan ends. A padlock means it takes a password.
4 · Nearby, end of the list
Other network joins one that hides its name. Scan again is last. Networks this device cannot join (enterprise, WEP) are left out.
5 · Password
Pressing a network with a padlock asks for its password, the field already active. It shows as typed. Enter joins; Join stays dim
until the length is one the network's mode allows. An open network joins on the press, with no screen.
6 · Joining
Join saves the network, set to join automatically, joins it, and comes back here with focus on it. The strip's fan shows while the
station names a network: on it, joining it, or failing.
7 · Connected
The network in use is its own row under the switch. Saved lists the others, heard or not; a press opens one. Nearby follows,
without what is already saved.
8 · Searching
No saved network in range, so the device looks for one, backing off between scans. Searching takes the network row's place and
is not a stop. No fan in the strip: there is no network to show.
A network
Pressing the network in use, or a saved one, opens its sheet. Backspace returns to the list.
9 · The network in use
What the link is doing beside the name. Join automatically is on for every network saved here; off, the device joins it only when
told to.
10 · Disconnected
Disconnect leaves and joins nothing by itself, the network kept. Pressing a saved network and Join ends that, as does turning
Wi-Fi off and on, or restarting.
11 · Turned to the end
Readouts are not stops for the wheel. Address is the IPv4 address in use. Forget is last.
12 · Forget
Confirmed, Cancel focused. Forgetting the network in use sends the device looking for another saved one.
13 · Wrong password
The row says why the network is not joined yet: Wrong password, Not in range, Refused. Getting address is between joined and
an address. A network picked by hand keeps being tried; one the device chose gives way to the next saved network in range.
14 · Its sheet
Change password comes first when the password is what failed.
15 · Change password
The old password is never shown; this replaces it. Save retries at once.
16 · A saved network
Join comes first, and joining one leaves the network in use. This one joins only when told to.
Hidden networks
A network that hides its name is joined by typing it.
17 · Other network
Name, Security (the modes this device can join), and Password, which goes away for Open. Join saves it as hidden, so the
device asks for it by name.
